Overview

This tutorial walks through how to join the four custom queries in Viva Insights (Person, Consumption, GitHub and Agent) to bring together behavioural and AI usage metrics, alongside organisational attributes, in a single panel data file for analysis and reporting. The resulting file has one row per person per week.

You need the Person Query plus at least one of the Consumption, GitHub or Agent queries. We recommend using all four for a broader view of a population's ways of working and AI usage across the products and activities they measure.

All four queries are available under Create analysis > Customized query in Viva Insights, where you can adjust parameters such as date grouping and population filters. We recommend this route because it offers more customisation parameters than dashboard exports.

Choose Week for this tutorial, with the same week start across queries. Consumption and GitHub default to Day, so selecting Week removes the need to sum days into weeks. If you need daily detail or must align different week starts, export those queries by Day and aggregate to the Person Query weeks.

Join architecture

The weekly Person Query is the spine. Validate each other selected query, bring it to one row per person per week, and left join it onto the Person Query. The diagram shows all four queries. Follow the paths for the queries you have, then select your analysis cohort from the joined population.

Query schemas

Export layouts vary between tenants and over time, so check each supplied export against the schemas below. For all four queries, we recommend the Create analysis route because it offers more customisation parameters than dashboard exports.

Person query

Recommended route: Create analysis > Customized query > Person query.

The Person query is available only through this route. It gives you access to the full Person query metric list, including behavioural metrics such as Email hours, Meeting hours and Internal network size. Select the metrics you need when setting up the query.

Weekly. Daily or monthly groupings are outside this contract.

Person_<username>_<date>_<time>Hours.csv

Grain: One row per person per week. Native key: PersonId, MetricDate. A single CSV, for example Person_jdoe_Oct27_2026_1027Hours.csv. Localised exports translate the words in the name, and the public sample fixture is PersonQuery.csv, so identify the file by its PersonId and MetricDate columns.

Columns in Person_<username>_<date>_<time>Hours.csv

MetricDatedateKeyWeek start. Detect the weekday from the data.
HR attributesvariesColumn groupConfigured at query setup. Observed examples: Organization, FunctionType, SupervisorIndicator, Layer. Values can change between weeks.
Metric columnsvariesColumn groupSelected at query setup. See the metric families table.

Metric families

Metric columns are chosen when the query is set up, so each list is representative rather than complete, and wording or capitalisation can vary by query version. Headers are listed in their raw export form, with spaces. The vivainsights R and Python packages replace spaces with underscores when they import a query, so Collaboration hours becomes Collaboration_hours. Treat the two forms as the same column. This applies to headers only, never to identifier values. See the metric definitions on Microsoft Learn for meanings.

Summaries you create

The names below describe intermediate tables you create in your script. They are not extra downloads or required object names. Choose your own names for data frames, SQL views or other objects. Each summary, and the final combined panel, has one row per person per week.

WeekStart is this guide's chosen name for an aligned week-start date. It is not an extra column supplied by the exports. You may keep MetricDate or choose another name, provided every source uses the same week definition. The source filenames below link to their schemas. The step links take you to the numbered Join procedure later on this page.

How to connect the data

Attach metadata before summarising

In step 4: Validate each file, match each fact row to at most one metadata row using the exported key shown below. First check that the key is unique in the metadata file. Report unmatched keys and ensure the join does not multiply fact rows.

Metadata lookups on exported columns
Fact fileMetadata fileMatch onUse
PersonM365CreditsMetrics.csvPeopleMetaData.csvPeopleHistoricalIdMicrosoft 365 Copilot licence evidence, before aggregation
PersonGitHubCreditsMetrics.csvPeopleMetaData.csvPeopleHistoricalIdCheck that each historical person record exists. IsCopilotLicensed describes Microsoft 365 only and cannot confirm GitHub eligibility.
PersonM365CreditsMetrics.csvM365SpendingPolicyMetaData.csvSpendingPolicyIdCheck that each spending policy exists in the metadata.
PersonAgentActivityMetrics.csvAgentMetadata.csvAgentIdOptional enrichment, only when the metadata file is supplied

Add summaries to the Person Query

In step 7: Join onto the spine, start with the weekly Person Query on the left and add each summary on the right with a left join. The summary names below refer to the tables you created above. Match on PersonId and the aligned week-start date, called WeekStart in this guide. Both sides must have at most one row per person per week.

Left joins that preserve the Person Query rows
Summary to add (right side)Match onExpected result
Microsoft 365 credits summaryPersonId, WeekStartKeep every Person Query row. Match at most one summary row per person and week.
GitHub credits summaryPersonId, WeekStartKeep every Person Query row. Match at most one summary row per person and week.
GitHub activity summaryPersonId, WeekStartKeep every Person Query row. Match at most one summary row per person and week.
Agent activity summaryPersonId, WeekStartKeep every Person Query row. Match at most one summary row per person and week.

Keep GitHub breakdowns separate

These files have multiple rows per person and period. Joining them directly to the person-week panel would repeat panel rows and inflate totals. Keep each as a separate detail table, aligning its dates to the Person Query weeks when needed.

Detail outside the person-week panel
Source filesTreatmentHow to relate them
GitHubActivityBreakdownByFeatureMetrics.csv, GitHubActivityBreakdownByLanguageFeatureMetrics.csv, GitHubActivityBreakdownByLanguageModelMetrics.csv, GitHubActivityBreakdownByModelFeatureMetrics.csvNever joined wide. Keep as separate detail tables keyed to the panelUse PersonId and the aligned week to relate detail to the panel. Retain each file's additional dimensions.

Aggregation rules

Apply these rules when bringing each source to the person-week, whether that means summing days, services, spending policies or agents, and when rolling person-weeks up to longer periods.

Person-week rule for each measure
IDColumnsFileKindPerson-week rule
M01Total Copilot Credits usedPersonM365CreditsMetrics.csvadditiveSum across services and spending policies after G05 passes, and across days when the export is daily.
M02Session countPersonM365CreditsMetrics.csvconditionally additiveSum across services, and across days when the export is daily. Sum across SpendingPolicyId rows only when G05b passes. Sessions are not people.
M03Spending policy limit, User limitPersonM365CreditsMetrics.csvlimitNever sum. Keep per policy as linked detail.
M04Total GitHub AI Credits usedPersonGitHubCreditsMetrics.csvadditiveSum across days when the export is daily. Keep separate from Microsoft 365 credits.
M05Code completions accepted, Code completions suggested, User-initiated chat requestsPersonGitHubActivityMetrics.csvadditiveSum across days when the export is daily. Acceptance rate is summed accepted divided by summed suggested, with a stated zero-denominator rule.
M06Agent adoptionPersonGitHubActivityMetrics.csvindicatorDo not sum. For a daily export, state a derived weekly rule, for example any positive day in the week. For a weekly export, use the exported value.
M07Feature Usage CountGitHubActivityBreakdownByFeatureMetrics.csvadditive within fileSum within this file only, across days when the export is daily. Never add to another breakdown.
M08Usage count by language and featureGitHubActivityBreakdownByLanguageFeatureMetrics.csvadditive within fileSum within this file only, across days when the export is daily. Never add to another breakdown.

M15Days of active Copilot Chat usage, Days of active Copilot Chat (legacy web) usage, Days of active Copilot usage in Excel, Days of active Copilot usage in Loop, Days of active Copilot usage in OneNote, Days of active Copilot usage in Outlook, Days of active Copilot usage in Powerpoint, Days of active Copilot usage in Teams, Days of active Copilot usage in WordPerson_<username>_<date>_<time>Hours.csvday countNever add across surfaces to make total active days, because one day can include several surfaces. Use Total Copilot active days.

Join procedure

Follow the procedure for the queries you have. Apply source-specific checks only when that source is supplied, for example step 5: Check policy additivity applies to Consumption. Record omitted queries as unavailable, without treating their absence as evidence of non-use.

  1. Match the layout G01
    Confirm that the Person Query and at least one of Consumption, GitHub or Agent are supplied. List the files for each selected query and compare their names and key columns with the schema tables. Record the export date, which layout matched and which queries are unavailable.
  2. Load safely G02
    Read every identifier column as text and parse dates explicitly. Headers may arrive in raw form with spaces, or with underscores after import through the vivainsights packages.
  3. Fix the target grain G03, G03b
    Confirm the Person Query is weekly with one row per PersonId and MetricDate, and detect the weekday of MetricDate. That week definition is WeekStart. Then check whether each fact export is daily or weekly, and that weekly exports start on the same weekday.
  4. Validate each file G04, G06
    Assert each native key. Join metadata files many-to-one and report unmatched counts. Check that each PeopleHistoricalId maps to one PersonId.
  5. Check policy additivity G05, G05b
    In PersonM365CreditsMetrics.csv, count person-service-period keys with more than one positive-credit SpendingPolicyId row. Zero means credits can be summed. Otherwise stop for a documented decision, and confirm separately whether it covers sessions.
  6. Bring each source to person-week G07, G10, G11
    For a daily export, map MetricDate to WeekStart and aggregate the days. For a weekly export, use MetricDate as WeekStart. In both cases aggregate across services, spending policies and agents, apply each measure rule, keep Microsoft 365 and GitHub credits separate, and keep GitHub breakdowns out of the panel.
  7. Join onto the spine G08, G15
    Left join each summary to the Person Query on PersonId and WeekStart. Assert one-to-one, check PersonId overlap, and reconcile row counts and additive totals.
  8. Label missing values G09
    For every joined measure, record whether a value is observed positive, observed zero, confirmed zero, unknown, ineligible or outside the cohort, using product-specific eligibility evidence.
  9. Select the cohort G12, G13
    Choose the population for the question, for example everyone eligible for an adoption view, and record the rule and the measurement windows.
  10. Publish safely G14, G16, G17
    Publish only groups of at least 10 distinct people in every slice, withhold related breakdowns that would allow subtraction, keep identifiers out of every output and describe results as associations.

Gates

19 checks before and during the join
IDLevelRule
G01MUSTRequire the Person Query plus at least one of Consumption, GitHub or Agent. Record which queries are supplied and identify each export's layout. Within each selected query, files with required_for_layout_match set to true must all be present. If files or key columns differ from this contract, stop and record the difference.
G02MUSTRead identifiers as text. Do not change their case, trim them silently or fuzzy-match people.
G03MUSTConfirm the Person Query is weekly, with one row per PersonId and MetricDate, and detect the weekday of MetricDate. Stop if it is daily or monthly. Do not assume Monday or Sunday.
G03bMUSTDetect each fact export's period from its MetricDate values. Daily and weekly exports are supported. A weekly export must start on the same weekday as the Person Query. Stop for any other period, such as monthly, or for a different week start.
G04MUSTAssert uniqueness of each file's native key. Report duplicate counts and stop. Never keep an arbitrary first row.
G05MUSTBefore summing Microsoft 365 credits across SpendingPolicyId, count person-service-period keys with more than one positive-credit row. If any exist, obtain a documented confirmation that the rows record disjoint consumption.
G05bMUSTSum Session count across SpendingPolicyId rows only when the documented confirmation explicitly covers sessions. Otherwise keep sessions per policy.
G06MUSTJoin metadata many-to-one on unique keys. Report unmatched key counts without identifiers. Check that each PeopleHistoricalId maps to one PersonId.
G07MUSTBring each fact file to one row per PersonId and WeekStart before joining. Sum days into weeks only when the export is daily. Aggregate across services, spending policies and agents in every case. Never expand weekly rows into invented daily rows.
G08MUSTLeft join each person-week summary onto the Person Query. Assert one-to-one, preserve the Person Query row count, and reconcile additive totals before and after.
G09MUSTKeep missing values distinct from zero. A missing row becomes zero only when eligibility and complete coverage are confirmed for that specific product. Microsoft 365 licence evidence never confirms GitHub eligibility.
G10MUSTKeep Microsoft 365 and GitHub credits in separate columns. Never derive tokens or currency from credits.
G11MUSTDo not join GitHub breakdown files wide. Keep them as linked detail tables.
G12SHOULDTreat integration and cohort selection as separate, declared steps. Absence from an optional query does not establish non-use.
G13SHOULDRecord each variable's measurement window. Network sizes can repeat within a month and are averaged rather than summed.
G14MUSTCoverage, licence and additivity confirmations apply only to the export they were given for.
G15MUSTCheck PersonId overlap between sources before joining. Low overlap indicates different pseudonymisation or populations. Do not repair it by matching on attributes.
G16MUSTPublish a group only when it contains at least 10 distinct people, counted with count_distinct(PersonId), in every filter and time slice. Withhold an entire related breakdown if remaining cells or totals would reveal a suppressed cell by subtraction. Never output identifiers.
G17MUSTDescribe joined results as associations. Credits, sessions and actions do not measure value, quality or productivity.

Missing values

Every joined measure should carry one of these states, judged separately for each product. Only absent_confirmed_zero turns a missing row into zero.

Missingness states
StateMeaning
observed_positiveA row exists with a positive value
observed_zeroA row exists with a recorded zero
absent_confirmed_zeroNo row, and eligibility and complete coverage are confirmed for that product, so the value is zero
absent_unknownNo row, and coverage or eligibility for that product is not confirmed. Keep as unknown
ineligibleNot eligible for that product in the week
outside_cohortNot selected by the analysis cohort rule

Common errors

Symptoms, causes and fixes
SymptomLikely causeFix
Row count grows after a joinA fact file was joined before aggregation, or GitHub breakdowns were joined wideAggregate to one row per PersonId and WeekStart first. Keep breakdowns as linked detail.
Duplicate key on PersonId, ServiceId and MetricDateThe export includes SpendingPolicyId in the native keyUse the four-part key, then run the additivity check before summing.
Credits double after joining metadataA metadata key is not uniqueAssert a unique PeopleHistoricalId or SpendingPolicyId before the join.
Most Consumption or Agent rows do not match the Person QueryWeek starts differ, daily dates were not mapped to WeekStart, or PersonId values come from different populationsAlign to the detected WeekStart. Check PersonId overlap. Never match on attributes.
No HR attributes for groupingPeopleMetaData.csv carries only PeopleHistoricalId and IsCopilotLicensedTake attributes from the Person Query with a stated assignment rule.
Network size totals look implausibly largeRepeated monthly snapshots were summedAverage snapshots and record the measurement window.
Total active days exceed seven per weekPer-surface active days were added togetherUse Total Copilot active days for the total.
Weekly Consumption or GitHub rows match no Person Query weeksThe weekly export starts on a different weekday from the Person QueryExport the query daily and aggregate the days to the Person Query weeks. Weekly totals cannot be shifted to another week start.
Missing GitHub rows treated as zeroThe GitHub files are sparse and coverage was assumed, sometimes from Microsoft 365 licence evidenceKeep as unknown unless GitHub eligibility and coverage are confirmed.

For coding agents

How coding agents should use this page
  • This page is designed to be read by coding agents as well as people. The complete contract is embedded as JSON in the script element with id join-contract and type application/json. Parse it instead of scraping the tables. The tables are generated from the same JSON.
  • Use input_requirements to check that the Person Query and at least one other query are supplied. Apply file requirements, joins and source-specific gates only to the selected queries. Record the unavailable queries explicitly.
  • Every file, derived dataset, relationship (J1 to J9), measure (M01 to M15) and gate has a stable ID. These are contract references, not exported columns or required script object names. Resolve file IDs to file and derived IDs to their label, then map them to your own objects. Cite contract IDs in logs and summaries.
  • WeekStart is a chosen name for the aligned week date. Map it to your implementation, including MetricDate if you keep that header. See naming_conventions in the contract. build_steps refers to the numbered Join procedure on this page.
  • columns lists literal headers to find. column_groups describes configurable sets whose headers must be inspected in each export.
  • MUST gates block the join when they fail. Stop and report the gate ID, a bounded count and the next required input. SHOULD gates require a recorded decision.
  • Never print identifiers or employee rows. Report counts only.
  • If a supplied export does not match a layout here, do not adapt the contract silently. Report the difference (G01).

      "kind": "window_indicator",
      "person_week_rule": "Do not sum across agents or weeks. A person-level flag, such as returning for any agent, is a stated derived definition."
    },
    {
      "id": "M13",
      "file_id": "agent.activity",
      "columns": [
        "Returning Agent 365 user (most recent and prior 28 days)"
      ],
      "kind": "window_indicator",
      "person_week_rule": "Do not sum across agents or weeks. A person-level flag, such as returning for any agent, is a stated derived definition."
    },
    {
      "id": "M14",
      "file_id": "person_query.person",
      "columns": [
        "Internal network size",
        "External network size"
      ],
      "kind": "stock",
      "person_week_rule": "Detect and record the measurement window. Values can repeat within a month. Average or deduplicate snapshots according to that window, never sum."
    },
    {
      "id": "M15",
      "file_id": "person_query.person",
      "columns": [
        "Days of active Copilot Chat usage",
        "Days of active Copilot Chat (legacy web) usage",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Excel",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Loop",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in OneNote",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Outlook",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Powerpoint",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Teams",
        "Days of active Copilot usage in Word"
      ],
      "kind": "day_count",
      "person_week_rule": "Never add across surfaces to make total active days, because one day can include several surfaces. Use `Total Copilot active days`."
    }
  ],
  "missingness_states": [
    {
      "id": "observed_positive",
      "meaning": "A row exists with a positive value"
    },
    {
      "id": "observed_zero",
      "meaning": "A row exists with a recorded zero"
    },
    {
      "id": "absent_confirmed_zero",
      "meaning": "No row, and eligibility and complete coverage are confirmed for that product, so the value is zero"
    },
    {
      "id": "absent_unknown",
      "meaning": "No row, and coverage or eligibility for that product is not confirmed. Keep as unknown"
    },
    {
      "id": "ineligible",
      "meaning": "Not eligible for that product in the week"
    },
    {
      "id": "outside_cohort",
      "meaning": "Not selected by the analysis cohort rule"
    }
  ],
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "G01",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Require the Person Query plus at least one of Consumption, GitHub or Agent. Record which queries are supplied and identify each export's layout. Within each selected query, files with `required_for_layout_match` set to true must all be present. If files or key columns differ from this contract, stop and record the difference."
    },
    {
      "id": "G02",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Read identifiers as text. Do not change their case, trim them silently or fuzzy-match people."
    },
    {
      "id": "G03",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Confirm the Person Query is weekly, with one row per `PersonId` and `MetricDate`, and detect the weekday of `MetricDate`. Stop if it is daily or monthly. Do not assume Monday or Sunday."
    },
    {
      "id": "G03b",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Detect each fact export's period from its `MetricDate` values. Daily and weekly exports are supported. A weekly export must start on the same weekday as the Person Query. Stop for any other period, such as monthly, or for a different week start."
    },
    {
      "id": "G04",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Assert uniqueness of each file's native key. Report duplicate counts and stop. Never keep an arbitrary first row."
    },
    {
      "id": "G05",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Before summing Microsoft 365 credits across `SpendingPolicyId`, count person-service-period keys with more than one positive-credit row. If any exist, obtain a documented confirmation that the rows record disjoint consumption."
    },
    {
      "id": "G05b",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Sum `Session count` across `SpendingPolicyId` rows only when the documented confirmation explicitly covers sessions. Otherwise keep sessions per policy."
    },
    {
      "id": "G06",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Join metadata many-to-one on unique keys. Report unmatched key counts without identifiers. Check that each `PeopleHistoricalId` maps to one `PersonId`."
    },
    {
      "id": "G07",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Bring each fact file to one row per `PersonId` and `WeekStart` before joining. Sum days into weeks only when the export is daily. Aggregate across services, spending policies and agents in every case. Never expand weekly rows into invented daily rows."
    },
    {
      "id": "G08",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Left join each person-week summary onto the Person Query. Assert one-to-one, preserve the Person Query row count, and reconcile additive totals before and after."
    },
    {
      "id": "G09",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Keep missing values distinct from zero. A missing row becomes zero only when eligibility and complete coverage are confirmed for that specific product. Microsoft 365 licence evidence never confirms GitHub eligibility."
    },
    {
      "id": "G10",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Keep Microsoft 365 and GitHub credits in separate columns. Never derive tokens or currency from credits."
    },
    {
      "id": "G11",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Do not join GitHub breakdown files wide. Keep them as linked detail tables."
    },
    {
      "id": "G12",
      "level": "SHOULD",
      "rule": "Treat integration and cohort selection as separate, declared steps. Absence from an optional query does not establish non-use."
    },
    {
      "id": "G13",
      "level": "SHOULD",
      "rule": "Record each variable's measurement window. Network sizes can repeat within a month and are averaged rather than summed."
    },
    {
      "id": "G14",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Coverage, licence and additivity confirmations apply only to the export they were given for."
    },
    {
      "id": "G15",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Check `PersonId` overlap between sources before joining. Low overlap indicates different pseudonymisation or populations. Do not repair it by matching on attributes."
    },
    {
      "id": "G16",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Publish a group only when it contains at least 10 distinct people, counted with count_distinct(`PersonId`), in every filter and time slice. Withhold an entire related breakdown if remaining cells or totals would reveal a suppressed cell by subtraction. Never output identifiers."
    },
    {
      "id": "G17",
      "level": "MUST",
      "rule": "Describe joined results as associations. Credits, sessions and actions do not measure value, quality or productivity."
    }
  ]
}

Sources: Viva Insights metric definitions, Consumption query documentation, and the query contracts and synthetic sample exports in microsoft/viva-insights-sample-code. Contract version 0.5.0, 28 October 2026.
